thread.title: Trump Warns Iran Over Qatar Gas Attacks, Halts Israel Strikes (For Now)
thread.title_full: Trump Warns Iran Over Qatar Gas Attacks, Halts Israel Strikes (For Now)

author: Mark Thompson
title: Trump Warns Iran Over Qatar Gas Attacks, Halts Israel Strikes (For Now)
text:
The escalating conflict in the Middle East took a sharp turn Thursday as former U.S. President Donald Trump issued a stark warning to Iran, threatening a massive military strike on the country’s South Pars gas field should Tehran continue attacks targeting Qatar’s energy infrastructure. The threats came after reports of an Israeli strike on the same Iranian gas field, and a retaliatory Iranian missile attack on Qatar’s Ras Laffan liquefied natural gas terminal, raising fears of a wider regional war and significant disruption to global energy markets.
Trump, writing on his social media platform Truth Social, stated that a U.S. Attack on South Pars would be of a scale “with a strength and power that Iran has never seen or witnessed before” if Iran continued to target Qatar. He simultaneously asserted that Israel would halt further attacks on the South Pars field – unless provoked by Iran. “ES WERDEN KEINE WEITEREN ANGRIFFE VON ISRAEL on this extremely important and valuable South-Pars field,” Trump wrote, partially in capital letters, according to translations reported by multiple news outlets.
The former president also claimed the United States had no prior knowledge of Israel’s Wednesday attack on South Pars, attributing it to “anger over events in the Middle East.” He further stated that Qatar was not involved in the strike, and that Iran’s subsequent attack on Qatari LNG facilities was “unjustified, and unfair.” These claims, however, have not been independently verified by other sources at this time.
Iran Strikes Qatari Energy Facilities
The immediate trigger for Trump’s warning was an Iranian missile attack early Thursday morning on Qatar’s Ras Laffan Industrial City, a critical hub for global LNG exports. Qatar Energy reported “significant fires and further substantial damage” at several facilities within the industrial city, according to CNBC. The Qatari Ministry of Defense confirmed the attack was carried out using ballistic missiles, and that Ras Laffan had been targeted previously on Wednesday evening.
Qatar, a key player in the global LNG supply chain, has condemned the attacks. Following the incident, Qatar announced it was declaring the Iranian military and security attachés at its embassy, along with their staff, persona non grata and ordering their expulsion from the country.
South Pars: A Critical Energy Asset
The South Pars gas field, shared by Iran and Qatar, is one of the largest natural gas reserves in the world. It supplies approximately 70 percent of Iran’s gas needs, making it a strategically vital asset. The potential for disruption to this field, or to Qatar’s LNG export facilities, has sent ripples through energy markets, with prices already reacting to the increased geopolitical risk. Deutsche Welle reports that world leaders are scrambling to contain the escalating conflict.
Saudi Arabia Reserves Right to Military Action
The situation is further complicated by the involvement of other regional actors. Saudi Arabia, on Thursday, issued a statement reserving the right to take military action against Iran if necessary, accusing Tehran of premeditated attacks on neighboring Gulf states. Prince Faisal bin Farhan, Saudi foreign minister, stated that Iran’s attacks were aimed not at U.S. Military bases, but at destabilizing the region, according to DW.
The current crisis underscores the fragility of stability in the Middle East and the potential for rapid escalation. While Trump has indicated he wants to prevent further attacks on South Pars, his explicit threat of a massive U.S. Strike raises the stakes considerably. The next few days will be critical in determining whether diplomatic efforts can de-escalate the situation, or if the region is headed towards a wider conflict.
The situation remains fluid, and further updates will be provided as they become available.
